name_reason: Name follows the convention data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> with domain=battle (sibling summon-spell-anim globals all use data_fd2_battle_summon_*). Descriptor correctly reflects both data type (byte = single uint8) and usage: 'aux_state' = auxiliary state, 'unread' = write-only (the only xref is a WRITE at 0x2657C; no reads program-wide). No Ghidra address residue: neither '_byte' nor '_unread' is a hex suffix matching its own address (0x53f7f) or any data address; they are semantic descriptors. Keep.
purpose: Write-only auxiliary state byte for the generic single-target summon-spell animation; cleared to 0 on INIT and never read back (vestigial scratch retained only to preserve the INIT store's target address).
logic_summary: Single byte at 0x53F7F living between data_fd2_battle_summon_spell_anim_phase_byte (0x53F7E) and data_fd2_battle_summon_spell_sprite_anim_tick_counter (0x53F80). The only access in the whole program is the INIT path (state_code 0) of fd2_tick_summon_spell_animation_state @ 0x26528, which writes 0 to it (alongside zeroing phase_byte and tick_counter) at 0x2657C and returns 0x1D. No code ever reads it back, so it has no functional effect; it is kept as a distinct named symbol so the INIT store keeps its original byte target. BSS zero-init; on-disk image is 0x00.
element_semantics: Single scalar byte. Auxiliary animation state slot that is only ever cleared to 0 on INIT and never read; functionally inert (a leftover/reserved scratch byte adjacent to the live phase and tick-counter bytes).
